text:
Predicates:
BornInMultipleBirth(x) ::: x is born in a multiple birth.
HasSiblingsBornTogether(x, y) ::: x and y have siblings born together.
ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(x) ::: x often complains about annoying siblings.
LivesAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home.
LivesWithStrangers(x) ::: x lives with strangers.
HangOutAndPlayWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
Party(x, y) ::: x is a party involved in y.
Year(y) ::: y is a year.

Premises:
∀x ∀y (HasSiblingsBornTogether(x, y) → BornInMultipleBirth(x)) ::: If people have siblings born together, then they were born in a multiple birth.
∀x (ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(x) → ∃y HasSiblingsBornTogether(x, y)) ::: If people complain often about siblings, then they have siblings born together.
∀x (LivesAtHome(x) → ¬LivesWithStrangers(x)) ::: If people live at home, then they do not live with strangers.
∀x (HangOutAndPlayWithSiblings(x) → OftenLiveAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend time with siblings, then they often live at home.
LukeBornInMultiple :: Luke is born in a multiple birth. (Expressed as a constant if specified)
LukeLivesWithStrangers :: Luke lives with strangers. (Expressed as a constant if specified)
LukeComplains :: Luke complains often about annoying siblings. (Expressed as a constant if specified)

Conclusion:
¬BornInMultipleBirth(Luke) ∧ ¬ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(Luke)
